introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. History 2 (0560), Paper 2 - Modern World History Since 1870, ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2019. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR Questions. TWO questions must be chosen from SECTION A, ONE from SECTION B and ONE other from SECTION C. One of the two questions chosen from SECTION A must be a Starred question. Maps should be used to illustrate answers where appropriate. All questions carry equal marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

In SECTION A, question 1 is compulsory in the following sense: answer either 1A* or 1B* (the two Starred questions) and one other question from the section.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION A: CAMEROON SINCE 1850**

Question one is compulsory. Answer either 1A* or 1B* and one other Question from this section.

**1. Either**

**A\*** (Starred question) Study this extract on petitions addressed by Cameroonian chiefs to British authorities in the 1870s and 1880s requesting the British annexation of Cameroon and then answer questions (a-e) which follow. (The maximum mark for each sub-question is indicated in brackets).

> The period 1879-1883 was characterised by a series of petitions addressed to Her Majesty's
> Government by Cameroon coastal rulers demanding annexation of their territory. Petitions
> were written in **1879 and 1881** by the Duala kings addressed to the British Monarch. A third
> petition was written in Victoria in 1883 by the native ruler and some missionaries to the same
> Monarch.
> Regrettably, Her Majesty's Government turned a deaf ear to all these demands for [margin: 5]
> annexation.
>
> The main task of the British Government in Cameroon was to regulate trade and commercial
> relations through Consular activities with the setting up of Courts of Equity and Justice.
>
> By 1884, the Germans and the French became interested in the annexation of Cameroon. The
> British and the Germans dispatched envoys to annex Cameroon. [margin: 10]
>
> The head of the German Government sent a confidential letter to the agent of the Karl
> Woermann Trading Firm. In the letter, he advised the agent to cooperate with her sister
> German firm in Cameroon to make concrete arrangements for German annexation by
> obtaining collectively from the four chiefs in Cameroon, the cession of the sovereignty of the
> whole area belonging to them for his Majesty... The German war ship, the **Moewe**, carrying [margin: 15]
> the envoy and his delegation will soon be with you... In their contacts with the chiefs, they
> should highlight the advantages they will have when protected by the Kaiser of Germany...
> **On 12th July 1884**, the Germano-Duala Treaty was signed.

**Source:** adapted from: *Cameroon: 1884-1985, A Hundred Years of History* by Victor Julius Ngoh.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a)
(i) Name the two Duala kings who wrote the petition to the British Monarch in 1879 *(line 3)*.
(ii) Identify by name the British Monarch to whom the petition of 1879 was written *(line 3)*.
(iii) Write down the name of the native ruler of Victoria who wrote the **third** petition to the monarch mentioned in (a)(ii) above.

(2+1+1 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a)(i)** The two Duala kings were **King Bell** (Ndumbe Lobe Bell) and **King Akwa** (Kum'a Mbape Akwa), the rulers of Bell Town and Akwa Town on the Wouri estuary. **[2 marks]**

**(a)(ii)** The petition was addressed to **Queen Victoria**, who reigned over Britain from 1837 to 1901. **[1 mark]**

**(a)(iii)** The third petition, written in Victoria in 1883, is attributed in the usual textbook account to the native ruler of Victoria, **Chief Manga Williams**, supported by some missionaries. **[1 mark]**

*Note.* The 1879 and 1881 petitions asked Britain to take over the coast; the Foreign Office did not accept (see the extract, lines 5-6).
themes: petitions to britain from cameroon coast

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b)
(i) Write down the name of the British Consular official who was charged with carrying out Consular activities in the area in the 1880s *(line 9)*.
(ii) In which two Cameroon coastal towns were courts of Equity and Justice set up?

(1+2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(b)(i)** The British Consul in charge of the area (the Bights of Benin and Biafra) in the 1880s was **Edward Hyde Hewett** (usually written *Consul Hewett*). **[1 mark]**

**(b)(ii)** Courts of Equity (mixed courts of European traders and African chiefs, used to settle trade disputes and debts) were set up in the coastal trading towns of **Douala** and **Bimbia** (Victoria is also sometimes cited by textbooks). **[2 marks]**

*Purpose of the courts.* They regulated trade, settled disputes between European traders and African middlemen, and gave the British a way to influence the chiefs without annexing the territory (informal control).
themes: british consular rule on the cameroon coast

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c)
(i) Write the name of the head of the German Government and the envoy he dispatched to annex Cameroon in 1884 *(line 12)*.
(ii) Write down the names of the two agents of the German firms operating at the coast of Cameroon who were to assist the envoy in the annexation of Cameroon *(lines 12-13)*.

(2+2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(c)(i)** The head of the German Government was **Chancellor Otto von Bismarck**, and the envoy he dispatched was **Dr Gustav Nachtigal** (the explorer, German Imperial Commissioner), who sailed on the warship *Moewe*. **[2 marks]**

**(c)(ii)** The two agents who were to help him were **Eduard Schmidt**, the agent of the **Woermann** firm, and **Johannes Voss**, the agent of the **Jantzen and Thormählen** firm. **[2 marks]**

*Context.* The two Hamburg firms had asked Bismarck for German protection of their trade; Nachtigal signed the Germano-Duala Treaty on 12 July 1884, a few days before the British Consul Hewett arrived (too late).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d)
(i) Write the name of the Kaiser of Germany mentioned in *line 20*.
(ii) Give any three advantages the Duala kings and chiefs were to gain if annexed by the Germans.

(1+3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(d)(i)** The Kaiser (Emperor) of Germany in 1884 was **Wilhelm I** (William I, Emperor from 1871 to 1888). **[1 mark]**

**(d)(ii)** Any three of these advantages (the Germans presented them to the chiefs in the treaty negotiations):

1. **Protection** of the Duala chiefs and their towns against rival European powers (Britain, France) and against enemies from inside the country. **[1 mark]**
2. **Protection of their trade**: the Duala would keep their position as **middlemen** between the European traders on the coast and the peoples of the interior, and would keep their trading rights. **[1 mark]**
3. **Respect of their land, farms and customs**, and of the authority of the chiefs in their own affairs (the treaty promised that their land, plantations and customs would be respected). **[1 mark]**
4. **Regular payments** (commission or "comey") and gifts from the new rulers, and the promise of development and order (end of disputes and of the unreliable "trust" system of the British traders). **[1 mark]**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(e) How did Cameroonians react to the German annexation from 1884 to 1890?

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The German annexation of July 1884 was not accepted by everybody. Reactions were mixed: some Cameroonians welcomed it at first, others resisted openly, and many moved from cooperation to resistance as German rule became harsher.

**Marking points (5 marks, one mark for each well-explained point):**

1. **Initial acceptance by some Duala chiefs.** King Bell and King Akwa signed the treaty of 12 July 1884 because they hoped for protection and for the safeguarding of their trade.
2. **Opposition inside Duala land.** Some chiefs and sub-chiefs refused to accept the treaty or felt cheated: the chiefs of **Hickory Town** (led by **Lock Priso**, Bonaprisso) and **Joss Town** (Bonambela) rejected German authority. In **December 1884** the people of Hickory Town and Joss Town rose in revolt; the Germans crushed it with the help of marines from their warships and burned the towns.
3. **Anger over broken promises.** The Duala complained that Germany was taking their middleman role, their land and their right to trade freely with the interior, and later sent protests and petitions (also to the British).
4. **Resistance of the peoples of the hinterland and coast.** Peoples such as the **Bakweri** (Mount Cameroon area), the Bakoko, the Bassa and others resisted German traders and explorers who tried to penetrate the interior; resistance continued throughout the 1880s and 1890s (the major Bakweri struggle around Buea came in the early 1890s).
5. **Cooperation and adaptation by others.** Some chiefs accepted German "protection" to gain guns, trade goods and protection from neighbours, and some Cameroonians sought mission schooling and jobs under the Germans.

**Conclusion.** By 1890 Germany had a firm foothold on the coast but had to fight hard for each region; the main reactions were limited acceptance, protest and armed resistance.
themes: indigenous resistance to german rule in cameroon
